techStack: pnpm, Express 5.2.1, TypeScript ~6.0.2, ESM modules (type: module), ESNext target
Zod 4.4.3 for validation — existing schemas in src/schemas/; validate() middleware sets req.validated
bcryptjs 3.0.3 — used synchronously (compareSync / hashSync) to match better-sqlite3 sync model
jsonwebtoken 9.0.2 — requireJwt middleware decodes token and attaches req.user = { userId, email, username }
better-sqlite3 12.11.1 — single synchronous db instance from src/db/client.ts; raw parameterized SQL via db.prepare().get/.all/.run
Vitest 4.1.5 + supertest 7.2.2 for tests; beforeAll runs migrations + seed; NODE_ENV=test uses in-memory SQLite
noUnusedLocals and noUnusedParameters are true in tsconfig — every declared variable/param must be used
features: POST /api/auth/register and POST /api/auth/login exist in src/routes/authRoutes.ts, handled by authController.ts via authService.ts
GET /api/auth/me exists, guarded by requireJwt, calls authService.getUserById(req.user.userId) — already reads userId from JWT payload, not URL params
UserRow: { id, email, username, password, created_at }; UserResult: { id, email, username, createdAt } — password omitted in result
No src/schemas/userSchema.ts yet; no src/services/userService.ts yet; no src/routes/userRoutes.ts yet
Custom error hierarchy in src/errors/index.ts includes AppError subclasses; 409 responses already used by register flow
errorHandler middleware in src/middleware/errorHandler.ts handles AppError subclasses and maps to HTTP status codes
rateLimiter middleware is mocked to next() in tests — must not interfere with new route
architecture: Layer order: src/routes/ → src/controllers/ → src/services/ → src/db/client.ts (raw SQL)
Routes export default Express Router; controllers are named-exported async functions; services are named-exported plain functions
app.ts mounts routers with app.use('/api/<domain>', router); new user router must be mounted at '/api/users'
Validation via validate(schema) middleware (src/middleware/validate.ts) — sets req.validated; use this pattern for PATCH /me body
requireJwt must precede validate in middleware chain on the protected PATCH route
Controllers wrap service calls in try/catch and call next(err); errorHandler translates AppErrors to HTTP status codes
Types for Express augmentation live in src/types/express.d.ts — req.user shape already declared there
New patchMe controller goes in authController.ts (per spec); userRoutes.ts is a new file parallel to authRoutes.ts
edgeCases: Spoofed URL params (req.query.id / req.query.userId on GET /api/auth/me): controller must read ONLY req.user.userId — currently appears correct but must be verified by inspection
currentPassword-only body (no username, email, or newPassword): Zod schema must NOT count currentPassword alone as a valid update field → 400
newPassword without currentPassword: Zod superRefine must reject → 400
Wrong currentPassword: service uses bcrypt.compareSync, throws 400 AppError 'Current password is incorrect' before any write
Self-conflict: uniqueness checks must use WHERE id != userId so a user can re-submit their own current email/username without getting 409
Atomicity: all checks (password verify, uniqueness for email, uniqueness for username) must pass before the single UPDATE fires — no partial writes
Password never in response: UserResult type omits password; updateUser must return only { id, email, username, createdAt }
bcrypt hash format after update must match /^\$2[aby]?\$/ — use bcrypt.hashSync with same salt rounds as existing auth (typically 10)
Only check uniqueness for fields actually included in the request body; skip the check if the field is absent
Unknown userId from JWT (user deleted): getUserById returns null — guard defensively before proceeding with update

tasks.requirement: 1 — GET /api/auth/me resolves user strictly from req.user.userId; query-string id/userId params are ignored
tasks.description: Inspect the me() function in src/controllers/authController.ts. Confirm it reads only req.user.userId and does not reference req.query, req.params, or req.body for identifying the user. If any such reference exists, remove it. No other logic in the file may be changed.

tasks.requirement: 4, 5, 11 — Zod schema for PATCH /api/users/me body: at least one of {username, email, newPassword} required; newPassword requires currentPassword; empty or currentPassword-only body → 400
tasks.description: Create src/schemas/userSchema.ts. Export updateUserSchema: a z.object with four optional string fields (username, email, currentPassword, newPassword). Add superRefine checks: (a) at least one of { username, email, newPassword } must be present — fail with 400-level error otherwise; (b) if newPassword is present, currentPassword must also be present.

tasks.requirement: 3, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 12 — updateUser service: bcrypt password verify and hash, uniqueness checks against other users, single atomic UPDATE, UserResult returned without password
tasks.description: Create src/services/userService.ts. Export updateUser(userId: string, data: { username?: string; email?: string; currentPassword?: string; newPassword?: string }): UserResult. Implementation: (1) fetch current user row with SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ?; (2) if newPassword is present, call bcrypt.compareSync(currentPassword, row.password) — if false, throw an AppError with status 400 and message 'Current password is incorrect'; (3) if email is present, check SELECT id FROM users WHERE email = ? AND id != userId — if a row exists, throw an AppError with status 409; (4) if username is present, check SELECT id FROM users WHERE username = ? AND id != userId — if a row exists, throw an AppError with status 409; (5) build updated field values: hash newPassword with bcrypt.hashSync if present; (6) run a single UPDATE users SET ... WHERE id = userId covering only the fields that are present in data; (7) fetch the updated row and return UserResult { id, email, username, createdAt } with no password field. Import db from ../db/client and AppError (or relevant subclass) from ../errors/index.

tasks.requirement: 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10 — patchMe controller in authController.ts: 401 without JWT (handled by requireJwt), delegates to updateUser, returns { user } without password, propagates 400/409 errors
tasks.description: Add exported async function patchMe(req, res, next) to src/controllers/authController.ts. It reads req.validated (typed to the updateUserSchema output) and req.user.userId, calls updateUser(req.user.userId, req.validated), and on success responds with res.status(200).json({ user: result }). Wrap the call in try/catch and pass errors to next(err) so errorHandler maps AppErrors to the correct HTTP status codes.

tasks.requirement: 13 — src/routes/userRoutes.ts: PATCH /me wired with requireJwt, validate(updateUserSchema), patchMe
tasks.description: Create src/routes/userRoutes.ts. Import Router from express, requireJwt from ../middleware/requireJwt, validate from ../middleware/validate, updateUserSchema from ../schemas/userSchema, and patchMe from ../controllers/authController. Register router.patch('/me', requireJwt, validate(updateUserSchema), patchMe). Export the router as default.
